attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Combines a present denial ('cannot do') with an unhedged, open-ended 'will never'. Treating it as a firm forecast with no deadline is correct.

contract.note: The contract counts LLM-based systems with external memory as 'LLMs' learning. Zitron gave no such reading. Ordinarily his denial targets the models themselves, so counting a frozen-weight model with a retrieval store as learning stretches the claim against him.

evidence.note: A dated 2026 preprint shows a frozen-weight agent improving through external memory. It is one domain, one run per condition, and has no independent replication; live reproduction needs a service available on request. Under a fair reading it does not show the LLM itself learning.
Test-time parameter updates in specialised embodied models. Reproduction package incomplete. Relevant, but not conclusive.
SEAL shows persistent weight updates on narrow tasks. It does not show learning from deployment experience.

reviews.rationale: The 'never' claim has no deadline. The main item (e1) depends on external memory with frozen weights, a broader meaning of 'LLMs' than Zitron gave, and is a single unreplicated preprint. e2 and e3 are narrow or incompletely reproducible. Nothing in the packet is a conclusive event that falsifies the claim under a fair reading, and nothing can confirm a 'never'.

attribution.note: Zitron's own assertion in his post.

semantics.note: A categorical present-tense claim that agents do not work at all. The normalisation keeps the 'at all' emphasis.

contract.note: The literal reading rests on the speaker's own emphatic 'at all' and his own working definition of an agent. The contract separates bounded task success from job replacement, so it does not stretch the claim. Choosing the quarter before publication is reasonable.

evidence.note: A primary benchmark (May 2025, inside the period) reports about 58% single-turn success, about 35% multi-turn, and over 83% on workflow execution. That is material task success, while it also documents real reliability limits.

reviews.rationale: The claim says agents do not work at all. The benchmark Zitron himself invokes shows agents completing defined business tasks at material rates in the period. That contradicts total non-functionality, though it supports his broader point about reliability and autonomy.

attribution.note: Zitron's own response line in his post.

semantics.note: The statement says 'burned'. The partner-capex qualifier comes from Zitron's own later explanation, so including it is defensible, but it changes the metric from cash burn to an estimated 'true cost'.

contract.note: The contract tests only the internal arithmetic of the speaker's own estimates and uses his text as outcome evidence. The claim is about real-world money burned. Showing his estimates fall below 4x does not show the actual amounts do, and the contract admits it does not test actual burn.

evidence.note: The speaker's own figures ($82bn and $77.1bn against $25bn) give ratios of about 3.3 and 3.1. That shows internal inconsistency, but his own statements cannot serve as independent evidence of actual burn.
This is the booster's quoted $25bn+ comparator, a premise and not a verified lifetime Uber figure.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no independent evidence of OpenAI's, Anthropic's or Uber's actual burn. The only outcome item is the speaker's own text. Its arithmetic falls short of 4x, but that is an internal inconsistency, not a measurement of the real-world claim. The gaps stated in the packet confirm the underlying figures are unverified.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps all conjuncts and the 'once built' qualifier. It is a broad generalisation about AI data centers with no thresholds.

contract.note: The readings are ordinary: operating jobs excluding construction, poisoning meaning harmful exposure, and an industry-wide scope. The target quarter is imported but reasonable. The vague terms are flagged.

evidence.note: The utility confirms 150MW supplied to one operating AI facility. That partly supports the utilities clause, but only for one site.
An advocacy group documents protests and threatened litigation at one facility, which supports neighbour opposition. Its pollution allegations come from an interested party.
The city's June 2025 short-term sampling found no dangerous levels. That weighs against poisoning but is only a snapshot. The later update was not used.
A senator's unverified claim of about 300 employees. It is an interested statement with no payroll support.
A 2024 study of Virginia data centers in general, not AI-specific: sparse but real operating jobs. It falls outside the target period.

reviews.rationale: The evidence covers one facility: substantial power use and documented opposition, while short-term air tests found no dangerous levels and job counts are unverified. The contract says one facility cannot establish the industry-wide pattern, and no representative data on operating employment, output, land or harmful exposure exists for the period. The claim cannot be settled.
